title: Many Hands
story:
NORA: SURVEY-QUEUE BACKLOG 412 JOBS
NORA: SURVEY-WORKER COUNT 1. EXPECTED 3
NORA: CPU HEADROOM 71 PERCENT. IDLE

The glacier survey pipeline (Compose project `survey`) has a `queue` and a single `worker`. The jobs are independent; three workers would clear the backlog before the shift ends. Amara tried to scale it and got a name conflict, because the compose file pins a container name and a host port on the worker. Fix the file so `docker compose up -d` leaves exactly three `worker` containers, and do not disturb the `queue`.
objectives: Edit `/workspace/compose.yaml` so service `worker` has no fixed `container_name` and no published host port
Project `survey` runs exactly 3 containers of service `worker` (via `deploy.replicas` or `--scale`)
startingState: Project `survey` is up with one `survey-worker` (host port 8200) and a redis `queue`.
hints: Compose names containers `project-service-N` so they can be numbered. A hard-coded `container_name` allows only one copy, and a fixed host port can be bound by only one container, so both must go before a service can have several replicas.

Delete the `container_name:` line and the `ports:` section from `worker`, then ask for three copies, either with `deploy: replicas: 3` in the file or with `docker compose up -d --scale worker=3` on the command line.

The worker section should end up like this, then run `docker compose up -d`:

```yaml
  worker:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    command: ["python", "-m", "http.server", "8000"]
    deploy:
      replicas: 3
```

files.content:
name: survey
services:
  queue:
    image: redis:7-alpine
  worker:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: survey-worker
    command: ["python", "-m", "http.server", "8000"]
    ports:
      - "8200:8000"

validation.description: `worker` no longer publishes fixed host port 8200
Exactly 3 `worker` containers are running in project `survey`

solution:
cat > compose.yaml <<'EOF'
name: survey
services:
  queue:
    image: redis:7-alpine
  worker:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    command: ["python", "-m", "http.server", "8000"]
    deploy:
      replicas: 3
EOF
debrief: Anything that must be unique per container -- a fixed container name or a fixed host port -- blocks horizontal scaling; stateless workers should be anonymous and reached through the project network. Pro tip: `docker compose up -d --scale worker=5` changes the count on the fly, but `deploy.replicas` keeps the number written down in the file.
